title: Isolation and profiling of viable tumor cells from human ex vivo glioblastoma cultures through single-cell transcriptomics
protocol: Immerse resected neocortical access tissue in pre-cooled (0°C) and oxygenated preparation medium immediately after removal from the patient.
Transport the tissue on ice as quickly as possible (<5 min).
Record the anatomical location of the resected tissue using neuronavigation software.
Keep the cortical tissue immersed in preparation medium saturated with carbogen (95% O2, 5% CO2) at 0 ± 4°C before processing.
Dissect away all visibly cauterized and damaged parts of the resected tissue.
Further dissect the processed tissue block into smaller blocks (size from 0.5–1 cm³) for sectioning.
Section tissue blocks into 300 μm slices with a dimension of 6 mm by 6 mm using a tissue vibratome (Leica V1200 vibratome) at a speed of 0.16 mm/s, in preparation medium.
Maintain the temperature of the sectioning chamber between 0–4°C with crushed ice during sectioning.
Bubble the vibratome containing the preparation medium with carbogen during sectioning.
Transfer 300 μm tissue sections onto Millipore inserts in 6-well plates, with 1.2 mL of growth medium in each well.
Discard the first two tissue sections from each block due to lack of consistency in section thickness (>300 μm).
Transfer tissue sections using a glass pasteur pipette into ice-cold incubation medium in petri dishes saturated with carbogen.
Incubate tissue sections for 10-15 minutes before placing them onto inserts for culture.
Refresh the growth medium at periodic intervals: First refresh 6 hours post plating, followed by every 48 hours until the end of the culture period.
Embed tissue sections in O.C.T. for H&E staining and immunohistochemistry.
Re-section embedded tissue using a cryotome for a final thickness of 10 μm.
Clean the vibratome with 100% alcohol.
Wash all spatulas and scalpels with Incidin™.
Place the vibratome outside the flowhood during cleaning.
Wear both lab coats and face masks to prevent contamination.
Sterile filter preparation and growth medium.
Generate fluorescently labeled GBM cells.
Transduce cells with lentiviral particles according to manufacturer’s instructions (M.O.I. = 10, 109 TU/mL).
Seed 5 × 10^5 cells per well and incubate overnight at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Prepare the transduction mix by adding required volume of thawed viral particles and Polybrene (800 μg/mL).
Refresh culture medium after 24 hours.
Assess the quality of transduction using microscopy after 48 hours.
Inoculate 1 μL of GBM cells at the interface of gray and white matter using a Hamilton syringe.
Trypsinize GBM cells and dilute suspension to concentration of 20,000 cells/μL.
Inoculate using the Hamilton micro syringe delicately to avoid tissue damage.
Wash the Hamilton micro syringe with methanol, ethanol, and PBS approximately 20 times between inoculations.
Inject no more than 1 μL (20,000 cells/μL) of primary tumor cells into a tissue section to maintain tissue viability.
Rinse sections with growth medium immediately after GBM inoculation.
Remove surface tumor cells outside the inoculation spot to ensure infiltrative tumor growth.
Check Hamilton syringe regularly for potential clogs to avoid failed inoculations.
Flush the syringe with 100% ethanol if any clog is noticed.
Monitor tumor growth every 24 hours using a humidified and temperature-controlled incubating microscopic platform (EVOS M7000 with onstage incubator, Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA).
Preserve sections of interest by fixing them in 4% paraformaldehyde overnight for effective fluorescence staining.
Prepare enzyme mix 1 by mixing 200 μL Enzyme T with 1750 μL Buffer X for every 500 mg of tissue.
Prepare enzyme mix 2 by mixing 10 μL Enzyme A with 20 μL Buffer Y for every 500 mg of tissue.
Transfer tissue into C-tube and add enzyme mix 1, then incubate at 37°C for 5 min.
Dissociate the sample within the C-tube for 2 min at 37°C under slow rotation.
Add enzyme mix 2 to the sample and incubate at 37°C for 5 min.
Repeat dissociation step as described in previous instruction.
Centrifuge the sample for 1 min at 350 g, 4°C.
Remove supernatant and resuspend pellet in 9 ml growth medium.
Prepare a 50 ml falcon tube with a 100 μm strainer at the opening.
Apply 1 ml growth medium to moisten the strainer.
Filter the resuspended pellet solution bit by bit through the strainer setup.
Collect and transfer filtered sample into a 15 ml falcon tube.
Centrifuge suspension in 15 ml falcon tube at 300 g, 4°C for 10 min.
Aspirate supernatant leaving approximately 100 μL in the falcon.
Resuspend pellet gently.
Add the resuspended sample to a FACS tube filled with FACS buffer.
Centrifuge at 300g and 4°C for 5 minutes.
Wash the samples by repeating steps 7 b and 7 c.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Keep approximately 100 μL of the washed samples.
Prepare FACS incubation buffer with DAPI (DFIB) by diluting DAPI into FACS buffer to a final concentration of 1 μg/mL.
Add 450 μL DFIB mix to the washed sample and resuspend gently on ice, avoiding direct light.
Collect 35,000 cells that are DAPI- and ZsGreen+ into pre-coated Eppendorf tubes.
Repeat the collection for a second set of 35,000 cells.
Pre-coat Eppendorf tubes with 4% BSA overnight at 4°C before use.
Fill each tube with 100 μL of FACS collection buffer before collecting cells.
Measure and confirm one set of collected samples with a 1000 μL pipette.
Filter the collected samples through 70 μm FlowMi Cell Strainers.
Centrifuge the filtered sample at 300 g and 4°C for 10 min.
Aspirate the supernatant, leaving a final volume of 45 μL.
Resuspend the pellet and use 10 μL of collected cell suspension for a 1:10 dilution in total 100 μL solution.
Mix 10 μL of diluted GBM cells with 10 μL 0.4% Trypan Blue.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Observe under the microscope to count live/dead cells and calculate viability.
Resuspend the pellet from step in the 45 μL supernatant.
Use 43.2 μL to proceed with the 10× Genomics Single Cell Library Preparation protocol (CG000204 Rev D).
Proceed with the Illumina Sequencing protocol (# 15048776 v09).
Prepare Master Mix on ice.
Assemble Chromium Next GEM Chip G.
Load Chromium Next GEM Chip G row labeled 1 with 70 μL Master Mix + cell suspension.
Load Chromium Next GEM Chip G row labeled 2 with 50 μL Gel Beads.
Load Chromium Next GEM Chip G row labeled 3 with 45 μL Partitioning Oil.
Run the Chromium Controller (about 18 min).
Transfer GEMs immediately after running.
Proceed to GEM-RT Incubation.
Store at 4°C for up to 72 h or −20°C for up to 1 week, or proceed to the next step.
Add 125 μL Recovery Agent without pipetting mix or vortexing.
Discard Recovery Agent and Partitioning Oil from the bottom of the tubes carefully.
Prepare Dynabeads Cleanup Mix and proceed to cleanup.
Wash samples 2 times in 80% ethanol using a magnetic separator.
Prepare Elution Solution I based on the protocol.
Add Elution Solution I immediately, incubate, and transfer supernatant to new strip tubes using a magnetic separator.
Prepare cDNA Amplification Mix, mix with samples.
Incubate in a thermal cycler following 10× Genomics protocol for cDNA Amplification.
Store at 4°C for up to 72 h or −20°C for up to 1 week, or proceed to the next step.
Add SPRIselect and incubate for cDNA cleanup.
Remove supernatant after magnetic separation.
Wash samples 2 times with 80% ethanol.
Resuspend beads in Buffer EB, incubate, and magnetic separate again.
Collect and transfer 40 μL samples to a new tube strip.
Store the working solution at 4°C for up to 72 hours or -20°C for up to 4 weeks.
Run 1 μL of sample (Dilution Factor 1:10) on Fragment Analyzer with High Sensitivity NGS (1–6000 bp) kits for cDNA quality control.
Prepare a thermal cycler and Fragmentation Mix.
Transfer 10 μL cDNA samples to the Fragmentation Mix.
Add Buffer EB and Fragmentation Mix to sample strip, pipette mix.
Transfer samples into the pre-cooled thermal cycler and proceed with incubation.
Apply SPRIselect (0.6×), incubate, magnetic separate, and collect supernatant.
Apply SPRIselect (0.8×), incubate, magnetic separate, and collect beads.
Wash 2 times with 80% ethanol, resuspend in Buffer EB, and collect 50 μL supernatant using a magnetic separator.
Prepare Adaptor Ligation Mix and well mix with samples.
Set up a thermal cycler and proceed with incubation following the 10× Genomics protocol.
Apply SPRIselect (0.8×), incubate, magnetic separate, and collect beads.
Wash 2 times with 80% ethanol, resuspend in Buffer EB, and collect 30 μL supernatant using a magnetic separator.
Prepare Sample Index PCR Mix and add the mix to sample tubes.
Add individual sample index (i7 Multiplex Index, Plate SI-GA) to tubes and pipette mix.
Incubate in a thermal cycler with proper cycle numbers based on cDNA quality control results from step 10 k.
Store at 4°C for up to 72 hours or proceed to the next step.
Apply SPRIselect (0.6×), incubate, magnetic separate, and collect supernatant.
Apply SPRIselect (0.8×).
Incubate and magnetic separate, then collect beads.
Wash 2 times with 80% ethanol.
Resuspend in Buffer EB.
Collect 35 μL supernatant using a magnetic separator.
Store at 4°C for up to 72 hours or −20°C for long-term storage.
Run 1 μL of sample (Dilution Factor 1:10) on Fragment Analyzer with High Sensitivity NGS (1–6000 bp) kits for final library quality control.
Normalize each single library to a “starting concentration” and combine single libraries to form a library mixture.
Denature combined library with an appropriate amount of 0.2 N NaOH and 200 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.
Dilute the denatured library to the final concentration with HT1.
Proceed on ice as much as possible throughout the entire library construction process to minimize sample degradation.
